headline: The guard yelled at Hegseth. Hegseth gave him a medal.
summary: Specialist Thomas Iglesias shouted the silence rule at Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his aides when a laugh broke out during photos at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Veterans Day. On Thursday Hegseth pinned the Joint Service Commendation Medal on him. "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist," he posted.

cover_question.q: Why reward the guy who yelled?

cover_answer: Because the guard was right, and Hegseth said so.
table_question: Would you thank someone for telling you off when they were right?

5-7.script: A soldier guards a special grave at a big cemetery, and the rule there is quiet, like a library. On Wednesday the man in charge of all the soldiers was taking pictures with friends, somebody laughed, and the guard shouted the rule at them. On Thursday that same boss pinned a medal on the guard's chest. The rule won, and so did the guard.
5-7.why: A six-year-old knows the library rule and knows a medal. The guard kept the rule and got the medal.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, and a soldier shouting at grown-ups could be it. The script moves it: the library rule they have been shushed under, and a medal pinned on a chest. The boss rewarding the man who told him off is the part to repeat. Expect 'was the boss mad?' No. He pinned it on himself.

8-12.script: A laugh broke out while Pete Hegseth, who runs the Pentagon, posed for photos at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. The sentinel yelled the rule: silence and respect. Two days later Hegseth pinned a medal on him. A referee calls a foul on the league boss, and the boss signs the card.
8-12.why: They check whether rules reach the top. Here the top man signed the card.
8-12.why_long: At ten they are testing whether adults apply the rules to themselves, and usually catch them failing. This is the rare clean case: one rule, the man who runs the Pentagon breaking it, a specialist enforcing it on him, and the same man handing over a medal two days later. Expect 'did he have to give it?' No. That is the point.

13-17.script: Graceful, or smart? A specialist yelled the silence rule at Pete Hegseth at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Two days on, Hegseth pinned a medal on him and posted "We love standards." Second: the video came a day after he beat an impeachment vote. Does timing change the medal?
13-17.why: Two true things: the right call, and good for the man who made it.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: the medal was the right call, and it was the best answer to a bad video a day past an impeachment vote. The script asks them to weigh grace against calculation without one cancelling the other. Expect 'so was it fake?' The report gives no motive, only that he rewarded the man who called him out.

5-7.q: Did the guard get in trouble?
5-7.a: No. The boss he shouted at gave him a medal and said well done.

8-12.q: Why reward the guy who yelled?
8-12.a: Hegseth said the guard kept the standard. The medal says it out loud.
A high one that rarely goes to a soldier as junior as a specialist.

13-17.a: Not in the report. He posted the photos himself with "We love standards."

13-17.q: Why does that tomb have a guard?
13-17.a: It holds unknown soldiers from three wars, guarded since 1948.
